# open-compute-mcp

`open-compute-mcp` is a Node.js npm launcher for the separate Python [open-compute MCP server](https://github.com/ellmos-ai/open-compute). It starts the configured child command and forwards MCP stdio. Real screen capture and input require an interactive Windows desktop on the MCP client's host.

## Install

- npm client configuration: command `npx`, args `[-y, open-compute-mcp]`.
- The default launch uses `uvx` to fetch the Python project from GitHub and requires `uv` plus network access. The backend requires Python 3.10+; `uvx` can use an installed compatible interpreter or download and manage one. Default ref is `master`, overridden with `OPEN_COMPUTE_GIT_REF`.
- Installing the npm package contacts npm. The default launch fetches from GitHub. An optional TTY update notice can check npm.

## Process and network scope

The Node wrapper uses local stdio as its MCP transport. It does not filter network access, scrub the environment, drop privileges, or sandbox the child. The child inherits the launcher process's environment and operating-system privileges. The Python server and MCP client may access other services according to their own behavior and configuration. The MCP client controls routing and storage of tool results, including screenshots.

Action modes, deny lists, window targeting, and signal behavior are implemented by the Python server, not enforced by this npm wrapper. Review that project's documentation and the MCP client's approval settings. The Node wrapper's test suite does not certify live desktop, provider, or network-isolation behavior.

## Related integration

- [Cowork Protocol Desktop Companion](https://github.com/ellmos-ai/cowork-protocol/blob/main/apps/desktop-companion/README.md): optional, human-started computer-use adapter using the separate Python Open Compute MCP server over local stdio. Its documented default uses `uvx`; this npm launcher is not a Cowork dependency and does not change the wrapper's process, network, or privilege boundaries.

## Tool inventory

The following 19 names match the Python project's README at commit [`762cb15042f144d31e99e5834f9508dc9769dd66`](https://github.com/ellmos-ai/open-compute/blob/762cb15042f144d31e99e5834f9508dc9769dd66/README.md). The launcher defaults to moving `master` unless `OPEN_COMPUTE_GIT_REF` is set; the running server's schemas are authoritative for its selected ref.

`capture`, `observe_filtered`, `capture_filtered`, `do`, `tree`, `click_name`, `invoke`, `list_windows`, `get_screen_size`, `watch_dir`, `push_status`, `rec_replay`, `signal_show`, `signal_hide`, `signal_status`, `signal_abort`, `chat`, `note_observation`, `talk`.

For exact parameters and version-specific behavior, use the Python server documentation and tool schemas exposed by the running MCP server.
